Rekindling the Verdant Era Chapter 136: Do You Want to Try Playing It?

The moment Ying Chanxi and the others started running, fierce cheers erupted from the first-year stands.

It was probably because of Ying Chanxi's presence, and also because among the girls in the first heat, there were no others from the honors classes for the time being.

It even led to students from Classes Two, Three, and Four cheering for Ying Chanxi.

When they saw Ying Chanxi cross the finish line first in her group, Class One burst into even more enthusiastic cheers.

And when Yan Zhusheng took the field and, under the teacher's guidance, stood ready in the third lane.

It wasn't just Class Eight, nor was it just the first-years. Even some sharp-eyed second-year students pointed in Yan Zhusheng's direction and asked, "Isn't that the girl who was singing just now? She signed up for the 100-meter race too."

This prompted a crowd of people to gather at the stands, some even moving closer to the first-year section for a better view.

At this very moment.

Yan Zhusheng's fame within the school, thanks to the Rock and Roll Club's brilliant performance, had suddenly leaped ahead of Ying Chanxi's.

Before this, although many first-years knew that there was a girl who was an amazing singer and had showcased her talent during the military training nights.

But not everyone would be interested enough in Yan Zhusheng to go to Class Eight specifically to ask about her.

The vast majority of people didn't even know Yan Zhusheng's name.

The same logic could be applied to Ying Chanxi.

Comparatively, the honors classes, which paid more attention to academic rankings, knew from the summer preparatory classes that there was a "great demon king" in Class One, who was also incredibly cute and pretty.

But students from the other parallel classes might occasionally encounter Ying Chanxi in the hallways or elsewhere on campus, a fleeting glance leaving an imprint in their minds.

But if they didn't actively inquire, perhaps after three years of high school, they would graduate without ever knowing Ying Chanxi's name or which class she was from.

They would only know that there was such an unforgettable girl at this school, and then she would remain forever only in their memory, with no chance to ever find out more.

"Give me my staff pass." Ying Chanxi had already walked back from the finish line, and under the gaze of many, she said to Li Luo.

"Oh." Li Luo took Ying Chanxi's pass from around his own neck, then watched as she lowered her head, so he very smoothly looped it over her head.

"I'm so jealous..." Xie Shuchen watched this scene, his tone sour. "If only I were Ying Chanxi's cousin too."

"Wouldn't that mean you'd have no chance at all?" Liu Shaowen said. "I don't need to be Ying Chanxi's cousin, I just need to get on good terms with her cousin."

"That makes sense." Xie Shuchen nodded in realization, then chuckled. "Then I have a much bigger advantage than you. Li Luo and I are in the same club."

"And who says I don't?" Liu Shaowen sneered. "He and I are pen pals in the literature club."

"I've even performed on the same stage with him!"

"I've eaten with Li Luo several times, have you?"

"We've been practicing in the activity room every day recently, spending all our time together, have you?"

For some reason, as the two argued, the tone started to shift.

Down on the track.

Just as Yan Zhusheng was doing stretches in the third lane, Ying Chanxi stood beside Li Luo and asked casually, "That song of yours, 'Chasing the Light,' have you let anyone else hear it besides me?"

"Only you and Yan Zhusheng, I think."

"So it wasn't just for me?"

"A new song has to be recorded." Li Luo smiled. "I had to ask her for a favor with that."

"Hmm... that's true." Ying Chanxi reluctantly accepted Li Luo's explanation. "Well, if you go to Zhusheng's house to record songs again, remember to call me. I want to listen too."

"Got it, I won't forget you."

After getting the answer she wanted, Ying Chanxi walked to the edge of the track and waved at Yan Zhusheng. "Go, Zhusheng! Let's get into the finals together!"

Although getting first place in the group didn't guarantee a spot in the finals, it was pretty much a sure thing.

The preliminaries were ranked directly by time, regardless of the group.

If one group was particularly incredible, it was even possible for all eight runners to advance to the finals, eliminating everyone from the other three groups.

However, the P.E. teachers had records of everyone's usual running times, and the four groups were more or less evenly distributed, so such a bizarre situation was unlikely to occur.

Hearing Ying Chanxi's cheers, Yan Zhusheng turned her head. After seeing Li Luo, who was standing behind Ying Chanxi, give her a thumbs-up, she waved back in response.

"Get ready." The teacher in charge stood at the start of the track, raised a small flag to signal the finish line, and then shouted, "On your marks, get set—go!"

The moment he finished speaking, a tall figure shot out, pulling ahead of the others by several body lengths and storming across the finish line in just over ten seconds.

Unlike the fierce cheers from the stands earlier, this time, many people were left with their mouths agape, still not having fully processed what had happened.

"It's one thing to be a great singer, but she's this amazing at running too? She's not a sports student, is she?"

"She seems to be from Class Eight of the first-years. I haven't heard anyone say she's a sports student."

"You found that out so quickly?"

"Haha, I know Niu Qingling from the Rock and Roll Club. I asked her, and it seems she was a last-minute substitute lead singer. So awesome."

"Oh, the original lead singer was Wei Duo from the class next door, right? I have a faint impression. I was wondering why it wasn't her."

Wei Duo from Class Three of the second-years was sitting in the stands, her face as grim as water, clearly in a bad mood.

If Yan Zhusheng had made a mistake during the performance, or if she hadn't been so stunning, it would have been bearable.

But now it was clear that she had been completely outshone. How could she possibly feel good about that?

After all, she used to think the Rock and Roll Club couldn't live without her. Now it seemed she was the one most suited to be replaced.

Seeing Yan Zhusheng's figure flying down the 100-meter track made Wei Duo feel even worse.

However, whether Wei Duo felt good or not had nothing to do with Yan Zhusheng.

She hadn't even thought about such things. After running the 100 meters, she ambled over to the starting line.

By this time, Ying Chanxi had already left to go to the gymnasium to guide the next competitors.

Li Luo, on the other hand, had finished his duties and had nothing else to do for the entire morning, so he waited here for Yan Zhusheng to return.

"Here." Li Luo took out the harmonica and handed it to Yan Zhusheng.

But Yan Zhusheng just shook her head. "I still have the 200-meter prelims around noon. You can hold onto this for now."

"That works too."

Li Luo's men's 3000-meter event wouldn't be until tomorrow afternoon.

Other than that, he just had his guiding duties about twice a day.

With nearly a hundred members in the entire student council, the work assigned to each person was relatively light.

After the two runners from Class Eight finished their 100-meter preliminaries, Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng walked together toward the Class Eight section of the stands.

"Here."

Yan Zhusheng sat down next to Xu Yinghuan, then picked up her school uniform jacket and patted the empty seat on her other side.

"Thanks for saving me a spot." Li Luo plopped down, took out the harmonica, and fiddled with it in his hands as he watched the ongoing races below.

Yan Zhusheng, at his side, glanced over and couldn't help but ask, "Do you want to try playing it?"

"Uh..." Li Luo looked down at the harmonica in his hand, as if the imprint of Yan Zhusheng's lips still lingered on it. "I'd better not, I'm not very good at this."

"I can teach you."

"...You really teach everything, don't you." With a speechless look, Li Luo quickly stuffed the harmonica into Yan Zhusheng's hands. "Why don't you cheer on the guys in the 100-meter race in a bit, play a few tunes, and give it back to me when you're about to run the 200 meters."

"Oh." Yan Zhusheng took the harmonica. Seeing that he had no intention of learning, she didn't press the issue, simply raising the harmonica to her lips and beginning to play softly.

"Huh?" Xu Yinghuan next to them heard the music and asked curiously, "Zhusheng, you play so well. Is this a song?"

"'Chasing the Light,' a song Li Luo wrote himself."

"Ah? The class president has this kind of talent too?"

(End of Chapter)
